50: A psalm of Asaph. God, Elohim, Hashem. Why are the names of the Holy One, Blessed be He, mentioned three times? To teach you that with these three names, the Holy One, Blessed be He, created His world, corresponding to the three attributes with which the world was created. These are: wisdom, knowledge, and understanding. Wisdom: From where? As it is said (Proverbs 3:19), "Hashem founded the earth with wisdom." Understanding: (Proverbs 3:19) "He established the heavens with understanding." Knowledge: (Proverbs 3:20) "With His knowledge, the depths were split." And so it says (Exodus 20:5), "For I am Hashem your God, a jealous God." Here are three names corresponding to the three attributes with which the world was created. Similarly, the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben say (Joshua 22:22), "God, Elohim, Hashem; God, Elohim, Hashem, He knows." Why did they see fit to mention it twice? Because with these names the world was created. "God, Elohim" with which the Torah was given. One might think one name stands alone and the other stands alone. No, rather both were created together. And so it says (Isaiah 48:13), "Indeed, My hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens; when I call to them, they stand together." This is the meaning of "From the rising of the sun to its setting." A flesh and blood artist creates an image starting with the head and finishing with the feet, or starts with the feet and finishes with the head. But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so. When He creates a person, He creates them all at once. And so it says (Jeremiah 10:16), "For He is the Maker of all." And it says (Isaiah 44:24), "I am Hashem, Who makes all." This is the meaning of "From the rising of the sun to its setting." And from where do we know that He created from Zion? As it is said, "From Zion, the perfection of beauty." The beauty of the world. What does "appeared" mean? "Appeared" only refers to light. And so it says (Job 37:15), "And the light of His cloud shines." And from where do we know that it speaks of this world? It says here "the perfection of beauty," and it says there (Genesis 2:1), "The heavens and the earth were completed." And when He destroyed, He began from Zion. And so it says through Jeremiah (Jeremiah 9:10), "I will make Jerusalem heaps [of ruins]." And afterward (Jeremiah 4:27), "The whole land shall be desolate." And it says (Micah 7:13), "And the land shall be desolate because of its inhabitants." And when the Holy One, Blessed be He, will renew His world, He will renew it from Zion, as it is said (Isaiah 2:2), "The mountain of Hashem's house shall be established."

"Not upon your sacrifices will I rebuke you." Rabbi Nachman said in the name of Rabbi Berechiah, "If a person intends to perform a charitable act, the Holy One, blessed be He, writes it down for him, as it is written: 'And your burnt offerings are continually before me.' (1 Kings 5:5) 'And Solomon's provision for one day was thirty measures of fine flour, and sixty measures of meal.' (1 Kings 4:22) Rabbi Yehuda said, 'He had a thousand wives, and each one made for him a royal feast, and each one said that he was dining with her.' (1 Kings 3:15) 'Besides from the deer, gazelle, and roebuck, and the fattened fowl.' (1 Kings 4:23) 'And whatever you raise up to Me is a burnt offering.' (Exodus 22:19) 'Not upon your sacrifices will I rebuke you.' (Psalms 50:8) 'For every beast of the forest is mine, and the cattle upon a thousand hills.' (Psalms 50:10) 'What right do you have to recite my statutes, or to take my covenant on your lips? You who hate discipline and cast my words behind you.' (Psalms 50:16-17)"
